2001: A Space Odyssey:
This clip from 2001 provides a perfect example of a computer that has been programmed to sound like it has been humanized, and the agency that Hal tries to use to prevent it from being turned off. There’s a slow burning tension in the time that it takes for Dave to travel to Hal’s nervous centre and start removing the things that give him life, including the use of sound or the lack thereof. During this time Hal tries to plead with Dave to keep his life, trying to conseil but failing to convince Dave to turn around and change his mind. The ending of the clip, where Hal loses its memory, its voice, and then recites the original song it was taught with near the end of its life, ultimately shows the emotional agency that Hal tries to portray to Dave, as a computer and an Artificial Intelligence system.
title: A Bicycle Built for Two Thousand and 2001
introduction:
A Bicycle Built for Two Thousand:
The first thing the listener can notice is the way in which all the voices come together to, one, create a musical Choir that is not quite in pitch, whose mish-mash of human humming creates something in which the human voice is distorted greatly to the extent that almost none of the words that the humans actually say is audible, yet also sounds human. The computer with their electronic synthesisers produces a sound that sounds in pitch, but that also sounds completely like something made by a computer, from the computerized notes to the robotic singing, the difference is a song that is much more easily decipherable and listenable, but that lacks the human component. In conclusion, this is a piece that combines musical performance and technology in a bizarrely intriguing way, showing the usage of human labour and technology to produce a unique and creative piece of musical art.
